title: MY GRACE IS SUFFICIENT.
paragraphs: MY GRACE IS SUFFICIENT.

Paul begged God to remove it.
Not once.
Not twice.
Three times.
And heaven answered with something shocking.
Not deliverance.
Grace.
Listen closely, friend.
In Second Epistle to the Corinthians chapter 12, the apostle Paul the Apostle opens a window into a secret pain he carried like a splinter under the skin.
He calls it:
“a thorn in the flesh.”

We’re never told exactly what it was.
Some scholars interpret it as a physical illness.
Others believe it could have been relentless persecution, spiritual harassment, or even chronic weakness.
But Paul describes it this way:

“A messenger of Satan to torment me.”
— 2 Corinthians 12:7
Let that sink in.

This is the same Paul who saw miracles.
The same man who planted churches across the Roman world.
And yet…
He limped.
The Prayer That Wasn’t Answered
Three times Paul cried out.
“Lord, take it away.”

Imagine the nights.
The frustration.
The question:
Why won’t You heal this?
Then came the voice of Christ.
Not the answer Paul expected.

“My grace is sufficient for you, for My power is made perfect in weakness.”
— 2 Corinthians 12:9
Read that again.
God did not remove the thorn.
He transformed the weakness.
The Divine Paradox
The world worships strength.
Jesus glorifies surrender.
Paul suddenly understood the secret most believers miss:
Weakness is not disqualification.
Weakness is the stage where Christ shows His power.
So Paul makes a radical declaration:
“Therefore I will boast all the more gladly of my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may rest upon me.”
Not tolerate.
Boast.
Why?
Because every crack in the vessel becomes a window for God’s glory.
The Thorn You Carry
Some of you reading this know exactly what this feels like.
The prayer you’ve prayed for years.
The struggle that hasn’t left.
The weakness you wish God would erase.
But what if the thorn isn’t punishment?

What if it’s protection from pride…
or a platform for grace?
Paul says earlier in the passage that the thorn kept him from becoming conceited because of the incredible revelations he had received.
God sometimes allows a thorn so our soul stays close to Him.
The Gospel Hidden in the Thorn
Look to the cross.
Jesus Christ Himself carried what looked like defeat.

Nails.
Thorns.
Shame.
Yet that very weakness became the doorway of salvation for the world.
Sin was crushed not by earthly strength—
but by sacrificial love.
And through His death and resurrection, grace flows to sinners who repent and trust Him.

That same grace that held Paul…
holds you.
The Final Word
Your thorn does not mean God abandoned you.
It may mean He’s doing something deeper than healing.
Something eternal.
Because when human strength collapses…
Christ stands tallest.
And His whisper still echoes through history:
“My grace is sufficient for you.”
If this message reached you tonight, take a moment.
Bring your thorn to Jesus.

Confess.
Surrender.
Trust the Savior who turns weakness into glory.
Because in Christ,
your worst wound can become the place where grace shines brightest.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
